cover_with: with Mike Agugliaro of FuDog Group

youtube.title: How a blue collar owner built a $32 million company, and what septic owners can learn

captions.facebook:
Mike Agugliaro of {fudog} started as an electrician who climbed in attics and dug ditches for wires. After about a decade of suffering, he turned it around. He took his company from under a million dollars to over $32 million in less than 10 years, with 165 trucks and 200 employees all over New Jersey, double digit profit, and he loved it. The last five years, he says, it ran without him. He did not even have an office in the building. A lot of septic owners have never seen what that looks like, and it starts in how you think about the business.

#septic

youtube.title: Septic owners say they work 24/7. Here is where the hours really go
You can't build a $5 million septic company with a $500,000 identity

captions.facebook:
I have heard a lot of septic and excavation owners say they just do not want to grow a big company. Mike Agugliaro of {fudog} hears it too, and he has a quick answer. Big company, big money. Small company, same problems, except less money. He says you are never going to build a $5 million company with a $500,000 identity, because you will not have the skills for it until you see yourself as someone worthy of it. The blue collar world is full of old thinking, and he thinks it is time to let some of it go.

#septic

youtube.title: Why septic owners should not blindly trust AI, with Mike Agugliaro
Can't find good septic help? Mike Agugliaro says it comes down to your thinking

captions.facebook:
At a conference, I kept hearing the same thing from owners: I just cannot find good help. Mike Agugliaro of {fudog} hears it too, and in New Jersey he asks, there are almost 9 million people, so did you interview all of them? He says the problem starts with the thermometer, the thing that regulates what you believe is possible. He does not like the word mindset, because set sounds like concrete poured in your mind. He calls it mind growth, and that is the part owners can change.

#septic

youtube.title: Can't hire septic help? He changed his thinking and hired someone that same day

captions.facebook:
Mike Agugliaro of {fudog} remembers telling one of his coaches that good people were hard to find and none of them showed up for work. The coach said, well, that is a great attitude to have, I am sure a lot of people are waiting to work for you. He said there are tons of people and Mike just did not see them yet. So Mike tried it. About an hour later his phone rang. A guy asked, are you hiring? Mike met him and hired him the same day. If you have been stuck on hiring, it might be worth a listen.

#septic

youtube.title: What your hour is worth: a septic owner's math on what to hand off

captions.facebook:
A lot of septic and excavation owners I work with are the busiest people I know. They answer the phone, answer the crew and work the job site themselves. Mike Agugliaro of {fudog} has a simple way to look at it. Figure out what an hour of your time is worth. If it is $100, then every time you do an $8 an hour task, you are losing $92 an hour. Someone else can usually do that task for less, and probably do it better. The hard part is stopping long enough to ask who could do this for you.

#septic
